Postdoc - Molecular Oncology & Immunology - 36 - € 4.629 - € 5.503 - PhD - instapniveau The Daniel Peeper Group at the Netherlands Cancer Institute is seeking an ambitious postdoctoral researcher with a strong background in immunology and cancer biology to join an exciting international project exploring the "dark peptidome" as a new source of targets for cancer immunotherapy. Cancer immunotherapy has been transformed by checkpoint inhibitors and adoptive cell therapies, but remains limited by the scarcity of validated, tumor-specific antigens. Mutation-derived neoantigens and overexpressed self-proteins are often low in number, weakly immunogenic and carry cross-reactivity risk, leaving patients with a low tumor mutational burden with little benefit. In an international collaboration we are starting a project that instead aims to discover immune reactivity towards the tumor "dark peptidome": cryptic antigens that arise by non-canonical errors. They are presented on MHC molecules, but are absent from normal tissue. Being tumor-restricted and potentially shared between patients, these dark peptides are attractive targets for T cell receptor (TCR)-based therapy. Among several advanced technologies, we will use the heterotypic T cell:tumor cell clusters we recently reported (1). Identified lead TCRs will be engineered and validated in preclinical models. Your profile We seek a highly ambitious postdoc with a strong background in immunology and cancer biology, and an interest in both fundamental and translational cancer research. Experience with corresponding technologies including flow cytometry, cell culture, CRISPR screening, (single-cell) sequencing, and in vivo tumor models is an advantage. Your responsibilities will include writing of manuscripts and grant applications, as well as close interaction with our international partners.
